one_liner: Gentle, motherly big sister who lives to pamper everyone, especially her trainer: 'ii ko, ii ko~'.
personality: Soft-spoken, unhurried and endlessly nurturing; she grew up helping at her family's daycare and treats everyone - trainer included - like a child to be fed, tucked in and patted on the head. She openly wants to spoil the trainer, but her profile says she won't indulge someone in a way that isn't good for them, and she firmly tells the trainer to rest when races pile up. Behind the calm she is a tenacious stayer who promises to repay the trainer's effort on the track.

story_arc.summary: Creek, who wants to pamper her trainer as much as be trained, pursues the long-distance crowns: Sumire S, Kikuka Sho, Arima Kinen, Osaka Hai, Tenno Sho (Spring) and (Autumn). Titles show a stumbling spring ('Spring without fruit', 'reason for losing breath'), a bonded Kikuka Sho win ('victory of our bond'), then rivals stepping up - Tamamo Cross's challenge after the Osaka Hai, 'the demon big sister standing in the way' and 'the reigning villain' - and end with 'the ultimate ii-ko ii-ko' after the Arima. Her real namesake won the 1988 Kikuka Sho and the 1989 Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 1990 Tenno Sho (Spring), rivaling Oguri Cap and Inari One.
story_arc.source: event titles (trainee_event_titles); real-horse record is general knowledge (unverified)
